about: The public projection of dossier/. Applied in order: exclude_records, derive, drop_paths, URL rules, templates, clause rules. Every change is logged with its rule id in the local store (strip_log). The source JSON is never edited by this file.

clause_rules.why: restriction wording; a clause that carries a number is a technical limit and stays

use-rights and licence wording: a use that a plan permits or forbids (commercial, non-commercial, personal or internal use), a vendor's written consent, a licence of data or content (CC BY, CC0, ODbL, PDDL, 'licensed under'), an attribution or redistribution condition, and a right to store, cache, share or resell returned data. Its neutralisers run on every clause it matches, with a number or not: they delete the phrase when a technical fact shares the clause ('100 calls a month, non-commercial use' keeps '100 calls a month'), and the rest stays when L3 no longer matches it and it keeps three words. A clause that is only terms is withheld, and one that still matches and carries a number is held. 'Personal use' counts only beside a word that makes it a right ('for personal use', 'personal use only'), because it also names a workload. A software licence (Apache, MIT, GPL), a licence key and a licence sold as a product (a Windows licence, a commercial software licence) stay. The pattern is a list of alternatives joined with |, and {NAME} in it stands for the part that defs names
a relative date: 'read today' means the record's verified_at, which is in its own field. Class tidy: the word goes and the clause stays, and check C20 does not count it

clause_rules.why: a pointer to a private file of this repository: a stored copy in sources/p/ or sources/c/, a record path in dossier/ that is not published, a script, a private document. It is correct in a private record and has no meaning in the public build, so the projection withholds its clause (or a neutraliser keeps the fact: probe.py -> probe). Class pointer: the projection applies it, and check C20 does not count it, because a pointer is not narrative. It runs after every N and P rule, so a clause that also narrates is recorded under its narrative rule

a path of this repository inside quoted text: no vendor writes one, so the quote is the corpus quoting its own notes. F1 reads the clause with quotes set aside; this rule reads the quotes too. Class pointer, as F1

a reference to a numbered rule of the research method ('rule 4 disqualifier', 'which is rule 6 in action', '(rule 8)'): the method is a private document, so the number means nothing to a reader. The neutralisers delete the reference and keep the fact it was attached to; a clause that is only the reference is withheld. A vendor's own numbered clause ('rule 3.1 requires') has a decimal and stays

personal_scan.about: A personal e-mail address or phone number in a published field fails the build. Unlike the token rules P8 and P9, which rewrite what they find, this scan reads the source value of every field the projection publishes (build.py personal_scan) and refuses the build, so the detail is removed at the source and not only hidden in the output. The same patterns are in leak_scan, which the public export applies to every file it writes. A role address, a placeholder and a login syntax that a service documents are allowed; a new one is added to role_words or documented_addresses in a reviewed pull request, and test_projection.py proves both lists pass.

boilerplate_values.re: ^(?:the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota|one stream is shaped, and the client's throughput is the shaped rate times the number of streams|the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else|the quota is real and unreachable: identity is the binding constraint, and it is not one of the six limits kinds|a clock, not a quota: bytes leave whether or not the client is finished with them)\.?$
boilerplate_values.why: the gloss of a binding kind, shared word for word by 530 records of the storage migration: it says what the kind means, not what binds this record, and the binding field and its vocabulary already say so
a source that names a private research document is no source a reader can open; the limit row keeps its value

title_rule.process_re: \bre-?verif\w*|\brevisit\w*|\bre-?probe\w*|\bre-?check\w*|\bcandidates?\b|\bprecedent\b|\bstructural note\b|^structural\b|\brules? \d+\b|\bin the set\b|\bin this (?:slot|slice|lane|set|wave|session|survey|batch|niche|class|family|group|category)\b|\breal lever\b|\bheadline\b|\bmultiplier\b|\bprice (?:anchor|floor)\b|\breference case\b|\bhonest\w*|\bcredible-looking\b|\bleast verifiable\b|\bcorrected\b|\bnot a discovery\b|^known$|\bfound anywhere\b|\bin the (?:family|group|fediverse)\b|\binstance found\b|\bfails[- ](?:quota|egress|identity)\b|\bqualifies\b|\bnot a candidate\b
title_rule.why: a provider, tier or category is the title of a page, a row and a search hit: the vendor and the product. The research left notes in some of them: a review state ('(revisit)', '(re-verify)', 're-verified write path'), a cross-reference ('see candidate entry', '(precedent, not a candidate)'), a numbered rule of the method, and ranking commentary ('the best ... in the set', 'the strongest finding in this slot', 'BYOB is the real lever'). A parenthesis that holds such a note goes; after the first spaced dash, the first clause that holds one goes with every clause after it. The vendor and the product stay, the name is never emptied, and the slug and the record id, which are permanent URLs, are never changed

truncated.why: a migration of the storage topic cut texts at 190 characters; a value of that length that does not end a sentence is cut back to its last whole word and marked with an ellipsis. The repair at the source is an rq:research issue. Other migrations cut texts at 300, 400 or 800 characters and ended them with the ellipsis right after a letter; such a value loses its last, cut word too
